_comment: Subdomain takeover fingerprint database. Each service entry describes how to confirm that a dangling CNAME (or A record pointing at a cloud provider's IP range) can be claimed by an attacker. Matching is done on the CNAME target (cname_patterns) AND/OR the HTTP response body + status code returned when fetching the dangling hostname. References: can-i-take-over-xyz, nuclei-templates/http/takeovers, Project Discovery and EdOverflow community fingerprints.

services.name: aws-s3
http_fingerprints: The specified bucket does not exist
services.description: The CNAME points at an S3 bucket endpoint that does not exist. An attacker can register the bucket name in their own AWS account and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: github-pages
http_fingerprints: There isn't a GitHub Pages site here.
For root URLs (like http://example.com/) you must provide an index.html file
services.description: The CNAME points at a GitHub Pages site that no longer exists. An attacker can create a repository with the matching username.github.io/project mapping and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: heroku
services.description: The CNAME points at a Heroku app that no longer exists. An attacker can create a new Heroku app with the same slug and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: azure-webapps
http_fingerprints: The resource you are looking for has been removed
services.description: The CNAME points at an Azure resource (Web App, CDN, Traffic Manager, Blob Storage) that has been released. An attacker can re-register the resource name and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: netlify
services.description: The CNAME points at a Netlify site that no longer exists. An attacker can claim the site slug on Netlify and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: fastly
http_fingerprints: Please check that this domain has been added to a service
services.description: The CNAME points at Fastly but no service is configured for this hostname. An attacker who controls a Fastly account can add this hostname to their service and serve content on it.

services.name: shopify
http_fingerprints: Sorry, this shop is currently unavailable.
services.description: The CNAME points at a Shopify store that is no longer available. An attacker can register the store slug and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: tumblr
http_fingerprints: Whatever you were looking for doesn't currently exist at this address.
services.description: The CNAME points at a Tumblr blog that is not claimed. An attacker can register the Tumblr username and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: unbounce
http_fingerprints: The requested URL was not found on this server
services.description: The CNAME points at an Unbounce landing page that does not exist. An attacker with an Unbounce account can claim the page slug and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: cargo-collective
http_fingerprints: If you're moving your domain away from Cargo you must make this configuration through your registrar's DNS control panel.
services.description: The CNAME points at a Cargo Collective site that is no longer active. An attacker can claim the site on Cargo and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: ghost
http_fingerprints: The thing you were looking for is no longer here, or never was
services.description: The CNAME points at a Ghost.io blog that no longer exists. An attacker can register the blog slug and serve content on this hostname.

services.name: surge
services.description: The CNAME points at a Surge.sh project that does not exist. An attacker can publish a new Surge.sh project with the matching slug and serve content on this hostname.
